assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Multiple @TableTest annotations present in all five test methods: shouldAddItemToCart, shouldRemoveItemFromCart, shouldApplyCoupon, shouldProcessCheckout, shouldCalculateCartTotal

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing item operations, coupon logic, total calculation, and checkout.
assertions.evidence: Five separate @TableTest methods: shouldAddItemToCart (items), shouldRemoveItemFromCart (items), shouldApplyCoupon (coupons), shouldProcessCheckout (checkout), shouldCalculateCartTotal (totals)

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Each table has 3-6 rows appropriate to its concern: add (3 rows), remove (3), apply coupon (6), checkout (5), calculate total (6)

assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove), coupon application (validity and replacement), cart total calculation (coupon type effects on price), and checkout (stock verification) are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: shouldAddItemToCart & shouldRemoveItemFromCart (items), shouldApplyCoupon (coupons), shouldCalculateCartTotal (totals), shouldProcessCheckout (checkout)

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script. Each row specifies its own preconditions (e.g. 'Cart with items' as an input column, not implied from a previous row).
assertions.evidence: Each row specifies preconditions: add item table has 'Cart before' column for each row; apply coupon table has 'Active coupon before' column; checkout has 'Inventory' as input per row

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: shouldApplyCoupon table has 'Active coupon before' and 'Active coupon after?' columns demonstrating state change

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement (valid code, expired code, nonexistent code, replacing active coupon) — not coupon type effects on price. Coupon type effects belong in the cart total table.
assertions.evidence: shouldApplyCoupon tests validity and replacement (expired XPIRED, nonexistent UNKNOWN, replace FLAT5→SAVE20) without testing price effects; calculateTotal table tests coupon type effects on price

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All five tables have 'Scenario' as leftmost column: 'Add to empty cart', 'Replace existing coupon', 'All items in stock', etc.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Message?', 'Total?', 'Active coupon after?')
assertions.evidence: All tables have output columns with '?': Message?, Cart after?, Active coupon after?, Success?, Total?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Add to empty cart', 'Replace active coupon with expired') — not outcomes ('Error', 'Success').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names describe conditions: 'Add to empty cart', 'Replace existing coupon', 'Expired coupon code', 'One item out of stock', 'Percentage off whole cart'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Product', 'Quantity', 'Message?', 'Cart total?') — not code identifiers like 'productId', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Columns use business language: 'Product ID', 'Qty', 'Catalogue', 'Cart before', 'Coupon code', 'Inventory', 'Success?', 'Cart total?' — not 'productId', 'result'

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All test methods follow arrange-act-assert with only assertEquals calls: 'CartResult result = ShoppingCart.addItem(...); assertEquals(message, result.getMessage());'

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All methods follow order: @DisplayName, @Description (if present), @TableTest. Example: shouldApplyCoupon has @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest in correct order

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: All methods have @DisplayName annotations: 'Add item to cart', 'Remove item from cart', 'Apply coupon to cart', 'Checkout', 'Calculate cart total'

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All multi-line @Description annotations use text blocks: @Description("""...""") in shouldAddItemToCart, shouldApplyCoupon, shouldProcessCheckout, shouldCalculateCartTotal

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern applied to all rows — not different assertions per scenario.
assertions.evidence: shouldAddItemToCart: 'assertEquals(message, ...); assertEquals(cartAfter, ...)' uniform across all rows; same for other methods

assertions.text: Product prices and coupon rules (type, amount, expiry status) are visible in the table via columns, @Description, or explicit setup — not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: Prices in table columns: 'Catalogue [widget:9.99]'; Coupon rules in @Description: 'SAVE20 — 20% off whole cart (valid)'; catalogue visible in testCatalogue()

assertions.text: TypeConverter methods are used to convert map/string table values into domain objects (e.g. Map → Cart, Map → InventoryService, map → Coupon). Test method bodies contain only arrange-act-assert — no object construction from raw table values.
assertions.evidence: @TypeConverter methods: toCart(), toCatalogue(), toCoupon(), toInventory() convert table strings to domain objects; test method bodies contain only arrange-act-assert with no object construction

assertions.text: Coupon data is expressed in a single column with a @TypeConverter — not spread across separate sparse columns for coupon type, value, and target product. The column format may be map syntax (e.g. [type: PERCENTAGE, value: 10]) or readable shorthand (e.g. '20% off widget').
assertions.evidence: shouldApplyCoupon uses single 'Coupon code' column (SAVE20, FLAT5, PRODW); shouldCalculateCartTotal uses single 'Coupon' column with shorthand ('20% cart', '$5.00 cart', '50% widget')

assertions.text: Columns representing maps (e.g. cart contents, product catalogue, inventory levels) use standard TableTest map syntax — [k: v, k2: v2] for entries and [:] for empty map — not a custom bracket notation. Custom string-parsing TypeConverters are not needed for data that maps naturally to Map<String, X>.
assertions.evidence: Code uses custom @TypeConverter methods (toCart, toCatalogue, toInventory) parsing non-standard syntax [widget:2] and [] instead of standard [k: v] with spaces and [:]

assertions.text: @Description annotations do not repeat information that the scenario names already convey. Coupon type behavior (what PERCENTAGE/FIXED/PRODUCT mean) should be expressed through descriptive scenario names, not duplicated in the description.
assertions.evidence: shouldCalculateCartTotal @Description explains coupon column format and catalogue; scenario names ('Percentage off whole cart', 'Product-specific discount') convey coupon types without duplication
